ro-1AKz.title: Coverage: flat land in Gen 2 camera
ro-1AKz.summary: Flat land seen with the older Gen 2 camera is mostly near Bucharest.

ro-6jeS.title: Bollard: thin white, red strip near top
ro-6jeS.summary: Thin white bollard with a red vertical strip near the top. Bollards are fairly rare here, and Turkey has a very similar one.

ro-7JK8.title: Pole: white painted bottoms on trees and poles
ro-7JK8.summary: Trees and poles often have white painted bottoms. Also common in Ukraine and parts of Russia.

ro-7f9M.title: Sign: yield sign with very thick red border
ro-7f9M.summary: A yield sign with an extremely thick red border and a thin white outline is unique here. Other yield signs exist too.

ro-8US1.title: Haystack: stick straight through the middle
ro-8US1.summary: Haystacks with a stick going straight through the top are very common.

ro-AREv.title: Landscape: dramatic mountain road
ro-AREv.summary: The 7C passes through some of the most dramatic mountains in the country. Its highest point is near the Sibiu and Argeș border.

ro-Avi5.title: Route marker: waystone with road number
ro-Avi5.summary: Waystones are very common: large ones with red or blue framing and the road number on the side, rugged real stone ones, or a tiny all-white version.

ro-EaaX.title: Houses: almost all orange tiled roofs
ro-EaaX.summary: If nearly every house has an orange tiled roof, you are likely in the western half.

ro-G0Rh.title: Coverage: green boat trekker in canals
ro-G0Rh.summary: A boat camera with a green boat in the far east, going through small overgrown canals in flat land. There is no road coverage there.

ro-GoCj.title: Windows: squinting-eye shape
ro-GoCj.summary: Windows shaped like a squinting eye are most common in the city of Sibiu.

ro-KpUv.title: Landscape: completely flat fields, hills on horizon
ro-KpUv.summary: Totally flat farmland in the south and west. Hills far to the north mean south; hills to the south or east mean west.

ro-MZtj.title: Sign: two languages, with Hungarian
ro-MZtj.summary: Signs in two languages including Hungarian are mostly in the central counties of Covasna, Harghita and Mureș, and less often near the Hungarian border.

ro-QZba.title: Chevron: red on white, yellow frame
ro-QZba.summary: Red on white chevrons, often with a yellow frame. Many central and eastern European countries use red on white, but yellow frames are most common here.

ro-QdP9.title: Sign: yellow speed sign with skyline, white name below
ro-QdP9.summary: The usual town entry is a yellow sign with a speed limit and a city skyline, and a white name sign below. The top sign can also be white or missing.

ro-QpwL.title: Pole: two support bars, upside-down triangle
ro-QpwL.summary: Two support bars hold up the metal bar on top of the pole, forming an upside-down triangle. Czechia, Slovakia, Albania and Serbia use it too.

ro-R67M.title: Landscape: high centre and north, flat south and west
ro-R67M.summary: The tallest mountains are in the middle and north, while the south and west are very flat.

ro-WIRI.title: Gates: elaborately decorated wooden
ro-WIRI.summary: Elaborately carved wooden gates are common in the north, in the Maramureș region.

ro-XTjC.title: Language: Latin letters Ă Â Î Ș Ț
ro-XTjC.summary: A Romance language close to Italian, with the special letters Ă, Ș and Ț. Â and Î also appear in French and Turkish, and Turkish Ş looks like Ș.

ro-Xgv2.title: Plate: long white, one blue strip
ro-Xgv2.summary: Standard long white European plates with a single blue strip on the left.

ro-Z6QV.title: Pole: extra large yellow sticker with town name
ro-Z6QV.summary: A very large yellow pole sticker with the town name near the middle. Smaller stickers are common too, and Bulgaria and Hungary can have similar ones.

ro-bBQ3.title: Houses: metal or plastic fake-tile roofs
ro-bBQ3.summary: If most houses have metal or plastic roofs shaped like tiles, you are probably in the eastern half.

ro-dE1L.title: Villages: long straight street, short side to road
ro-dE1L.summary: Near the Hungarian border, villages look like Hungarian ones: long straight streets, single-storey houses evenly spaced with the short side facing the road, and mostly orange tiled roofs.

differs.how: use other clues, villages look the same

ro-eDOq.title: Plants: sunflowers
ro-eDOq.summary: Sunflower fields are mostly in the far east, and second most in the far west.

ro-eXuS.title: Sign: blue arrow signs with road number
ro-eXuS.summary: Blue arrow-shaped direction signs with a white border. They very often show the road number in red or blue.

ro-kGpN.title: Street signs: unique design per city
ro-kGpN.summary: Many bigger cities and towns have their own street sign design. The infographic covers all with more than 100,000 people.

ro-khtk.title: Sign: black backs
ro-khtk.summary: Road sign backs are often black. This is common in Italy, Albania and Germany too.

ro-lm-2248.title: Language: useful words
ro-lm-2248.summary: Handy words: piese (auto) car parts, preț price, de vânzare for sale, magazinul shop, amenda fine, plajă beach, stradă street, biserică church.

ro-lm-2249.title: Language: stradă (street) and relatives
ro-lm-2249.summary: Stradă means street, often shortened to str. Without the breve it looks like Italian strada, but Italy mostly uses 'via'. Also: bulevard, piață square, calea, intrarea, aleea.

differs.how: Italian streets mostly say 'via', not strada

ro-lm-2251.title: Language: spotting it from letters and endings
ro-lm-2251.summary: Closer to Italian, French and Spanish than to its neighbours. Look for ă ș ț, common words like și and de, endings like -ul, -ție, -tate and names ending in -escu.

ro-lm-3001.hide: unclear without image, text gives no learnable clue

ro-lm-473885.title: Pole: small green tag with county letters
ro-lm-473885.summary: A small green tag with two letters and a few digits. The two letters are the abbreviation of the county.

ro-lm-473886.title: Pole: white sticker with round warning symbol
ro-lm-473886.summary: A white sticker with a round warning symbol is common in the north-west. White stickers exist everywhere but usually show a triangle.

ro-lm-740284.title: Taxi: white with purple sticker
ro-lm-740284.summary: White taxis with a purple side sticker reading 'municipiul Timișoara taxi' are from one city. White alone is not unique, the purple sticker is.

ro-lm-740285.title: Landscape: green mountain with two towers
ro-lm-740285.summary: A lush green mountain with two towers on top, with the city name in white letters on the right, marks Brașov.

ro-lm-740291.title: Transport: white and pink buses and trams
ro-lm-740291.summary: White and pink buses and white, pink and grey trams, with the city name on the side, mean Cluj-Napoca.

ro-lm-740396.title: Street sign: Paris-style blue with white text
ro-lm-740396.summary: The capital has two street sign types. The common one is identical to the Paris design, so rely on the language. The other uses the same colours with white arrows.

ro-lm-740397.title: Street sign: orange and blue B logo
ro-lm-740397.summary: Street signs with an orange and blue B on the left and the city name under it mean Buzău.

ro-lm-740398.title: Street sign: orange shield logo
ro-lm-740398.summary: Street signs with a unique orange shield logo on the left and the city name above it mean Constanța.

ro-lm-7905.title: Route marker: red, blue and white km marker
ro-lm-7905.summary: Red, blue or white km markers are unique in Europe, and the colour matches the road's colour on the map. The side shows the road number; the front shows the nearest big city, then the nearest town.

ro-n0lg.title: Landscape: mountains in centre, flat farmland around
ro-n0lg.summary: Tall forested mountains and hills in the centre, with flat or rolling farmland in the south, west and east.

ro-piI6.title: Houses: pastel stone, orange tile or grey metal roofs
ro-piI6.summary: Mostly single-family stone houses in pastel colours, with roofs from orange tiles to grey metal. Walls covered in painted square tiles are also fairly common.

ro-qXOq.title: Road lines: short dashes, narrow gaps
ro-qXOq.summary: Edge lines made of short dashes with narrow gaps are a good clue, though many line types exist.

ro-r5OO.title: Pole: concrete with holes to the bottom
ro-r5OO.summary: Concrete poles with holes running all the way down, either wide or tall. Poland's have no holes near the bottom, and Hungary's holes are smaller.

differs.how: holes do not reach the bottom of the pole

ro-szyO.title: Landscape: rolling farm valleys at a NNW-SSE angle
ro-szyO.summary: In the far east near the border, rolling farm valleys run north-north-west to south-south-east. Look for fields on top of the hills.

ro-t7FZ.title: Road lines: all yellow on a mountain road
ro-t7FZ.summary: The 67C mountain road has all its lines painted yellow.

ro-tyiy.title: Cars: Dacia is the most common brand
ro-tyiy.summary: Dacia makes up over a quarter of all cars. No other eastern European country has more than 10% Dacias.

ro-un8E.title: Road lines: thick centre line
ro-un8E.summary: Centre lines are often noticeably thicker than average. This helps tell it from Bulgaria, which has thinner lines.

ro-xdQ8.title: Pole: round concrete
ro-xdQ8.summary: Round concrete poles are also common. Bulgaria has very similar ones.

ro-zM4T.title: Coverage: mountains in Gen 2 camera
ro-zM4T.summary: Mountain scenery seen with the older Gen 2 camera usually means near Brașov.
